background:
2 Peter: The Letter, Its World and Your Notes

Study notes · dates are approximate and scholars vary

At a glance

2 Peter is a farewell letter. Knowing his death is near (1:14), Peter reminds believers of the truth, warns against false teachers who deny Christ's return and live immorally, and urges them to grow in grace. Traditionally it dates to about AD 64–67, shortly before Peter's execution in Rome.

QuestionTraditional viewNotes
Author“Simon Peter, a servant and apostle of Jesus Christ” (1:1)The most debated authorship in the New Testament; many scholars date it later, about AD 80–120. The traditional view holds that Peter wrote it, perhaps with a different scribe from 1 Peter.
DateAbout AD 64–67Just before Peter's martyrdom under Nero, on the traditional view.
RecipientsThose who share “a like precious faith” (1:1)Probably the same readers as 1 Peter, since this is “the second epistle” (3:1).
OccasionFalse teachers and scoffersThey denied the Lord's return and promised freedom while living in corruption (2:19; 3:3–4).
Relation to Jude2 Peter 2 closely resembles JudeOne probably drew on the other, or both on a common source.
Paul's lettersCalled “scriptures” (3:15–16)Evidence that Paul's letters were already being collected and read widely.

The letter is framed by growth: “adding on your part all diligence” (1:5) and “grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ” (3:18).

Rome and the false teachers

2 Peter answers teachers who mixed Christian language with popular Greek ideas and Roman indulgence.

  • Nero's last years. After the fire of AD 64 Christians in Rome faced execution. Peter writes knowing he will soon die (1:14).
  • Eyewitness testimony. Against the charge of “cunningly devised fables” (myths), Peter insists he was an eyewitness of Christ's majesty on the holy mountain (1:16–18).
  • Scoffers. The false teachers mocked: “Where is the promise of his coming?” (3:4). Some Greek philosophers, especially Epicureans, denied divine judgment and taught that the gods do not intervene in the world.
  • Licentious freedom. They promised liberty while being slaves of corruption (2:19), indulging in feasting and immorality (2:13–14), much like the banquets of the Roman elite.
  • Greed. Like Balaam, they followed “the hire of wrong-doing” (2:15), teaching for profit.
  • Fire. Peter describes the heavens and earth reserved for fire (3:7, 10–12). Readers in Rome had just watched their city burn.

Peter explains the delay of Christ's return: “The Lord is not slack concerning his promise… but is longsuffering to you-ward, not wishing that any should perish” (3:9).

From the holy mount to Rome

2 Peter looks back to Galilee and forward to Peter's death in Rome.

  • The holy mount. Peter, James and John saw Jesus transfigured on a high mountain in Galilee or the north, traditionally Mount Tabor (or Mount Hermon).
  • Capernaum. Peter's home on the Sea of Galilee, where Jesus often stayed (Mark 1:29).
  • Rome. Where Peter lived his last years and, by tradition, was crucified during Nero's persecution.
  • St. Peter's. The Vatican basilica stands over a cemetery where, by early tradition, Peter was buried; a memorial there dates to about AD 160.
  • Paul's letters. Peter mentions “all his epistles” (3:16); Paul's letters were being copied and shared among churches.
  • The readers. Probably the churches of Asia Minor addressed in 1 Peter (3:1).

The time map

The shaded band marks the traditional date. Peter knew his “tabernacle” would soon be put off, “even as our Lord Jesus Christ signified unto me” (1:14).

Around the world in AD 64–67

2 Peter was written as the Roman world entered upheaval.

RegionWhat was happening

How the setting shapes the study

2 Peter answers ideas and conditions of its day.

PassageConnection to the times
2 Pet 1:4“Partakers of the divine nature”: Greek religion spoke of sharing divinity; Peter roots it in God's promises.
2 Pet 1:14Peter's “tabernacle” (tent) is his body, soon to be put off, as Jesus foretold.
2 Pet 1:16“Cunningly devised fables”: Greek myths about the gods; Peter claims eyewitness testimony.
2 Pet 2:4“Tartarus” (ASV margin) was the Greek name for the deepest underworld.
2 Pet 2:13Revelry in daytime and luxurious feasting marked Roman banquets.
2 Pet 2:19“Servants of corruption”: in a slave society, freedom and slavery were vivid images.
2 Pet 3:4Epicurean philosophers denied that the gods intervene or judge.
2 Pet 3:10Rome had just been devastated by fire.
2 Pet 3:15–16Paul's letters were already circulating and treated as Scripture.

Against teachers promising freedom without holiness, Peter calls believers to “holy living and godliness” as they wait for new heavens and a new earth (3:11–13).

items.text: Greeting
Simon Peter, a servant and apostle of Jesus Christ, to them that have obtained a like precious faith with us in the righteousness of our God and the Saviour Jesus Christ:
Grace to you and peace be multiplied in the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord;
Make Your Calling and Election Sure
seeing that his divine power hath granted unto us all things that pertain unto life and godliness, through the knowledge of him that called us by his own glory and virtue;

whereby he hath granted unto us his precious and exceeding great promises; that through these ye may become partakers of the divine nature, having escaped from the corruption that is in the world by lust.
Yea, and for this very cause adding on your part all diligence, in your faith supply virtue; and in your virtue knowledge;
and in your knowledge self-control; and in your self-control patience; and in your patience godliness;
and in your godliness brotherly kindness; and in your brotherly kindness love.
For if these things are yours and abound, they make you to be not idle nor unfruitful unto the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
For he that lacketh these things is blind, seeing only what is near, having forgotten the cleansing from his old sins.
Wherefore, brethren, give the more diligence to make your calling and election sure: for if ye do these things, ye shall never stumble:
for thus shall be richly supplied unto you the entrance into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ.
Eyewitnesses of Christ's Majesty
Wherefore I shall be ready always to put you in remembrance of these things, though ye know them, and are established in the truth which is with you.
And I think it right, as long as I am in this tabernacle, to stir you up by putting you in remembrance;
knowing that the putting off of my tabernacle cometh swiftly, even as our Lord Jesus Christ signified unto me.
Yea, I will give diligence that at every time ye may be able after my decease to call these things to remembrance.
For we did not follow cunningly devised fables, when we made known unto you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, but we were eyewitnesses of his majesty.
For he received from God the Father honor and glory, when there was borne such a voice to him by the Majestic Glory, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased:
and this voice we ourselves heard borne out of heaven, when we were with him in the holy mount.
And we have the word of prophecy made more sure; whereunto ye do well that ye take heed, as unto a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day-star arise in your hearts:
knowing this first, that no prophecy of scripture is of private interpretation.
For no prophecy ever came by the will of man: but men spake from God, being moved by the Holy Spirit.

summary.title: CHAPTER 1 IN SUMMARY
paras: Peter greets those who have received a faith as precious as the apostles'. God's divine power has given us everything needed for life and godliness through knowing Christ, and through His great promises we may share in the divine nature, escaping the world's corruption. So believers must add to their faith virtue, knowledge, self-control, patience, godliness, brotherly kindness and love; if these grow, they will be fruitful, and by them they make their calling and election sure.

Peter intends to keep reminding them, knowing that he must soon put off his “tabernacle,” as Christ made clear to him. He and the other apostles did not follow cunningly devised fables when they made known Christ's power and coming; they were eyewitnesses of His majesty and heard the Father's voice on the holy mount: “This is my beloved Son.” They also have the prophetic word made more sure, a lamp shining in a dark place, for no prophecy ever came by the will of man, “but men spake from God, being moved by the Holy Spirit.”

questions.label: OBSERVE
questions.text: What qualities does Peter urge believers to add to their faith in vv. 5–7, and what eyewitness experience does he recall in vv. 16–18?

questions.label: THEN
questions.text: Writing near the end of his life (v. 14), why would Peter stress that the apostles did not follow “cunningly devised fables” (v. 16)?

questions.label: NOW
questions.text: Which quality in the list of vv. 5–7 seems most lacking in your life right now, and how might it begin to grow?

items.text: False Teachers Will Arise

But there arose false prophets also among the people, as among you also there shall be false teachers, who shall privily bring in destructive heresies, denying even the Master that bought them, bringing upon themselves swift destruction.
And many shall follow their lascivious doings; by reason of whom the way of the truth shall be evil spoken of.
And in covetousness shall they with feigned words make merchandise of you: whose sentence now from of old lingereth not, and their destruction slumbereth not.
God Knows How to Judge and to Rescue
For if God spared not angels when they sinned, but cast them down to hell, and committed them to pits of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment;
and spared not the ancient world, but preserved Noah with seven others, a preacher of righteousness, when he brought a flood upon the world of the ungodly;
and turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah into ashes condemned them with an overthrow, having made them an example unto those that should live ungodly;
and delivered righteous Lot, sore distressed by the lascivious life of the wicked
(for that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their lawless deeds):
the Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptation, and to keep the unrighteous under punishment unto the day of judgment;
but chiefly them that walk after the flesh in the lust of defilement, and despise dominion. Daring, self-willed, they tremble not to rail at dignities:
The Character of False Teachers
whereas angels, though greater in might and power, bring not a railing judgment against them before the Lord.
But these, as creatures without reason, born mere animals to be taken and destroyed, railing in matters whereof they are ignorant, shall in their destroying surely be destroyed,
suffering wrong as the hire of wrong-doing; men that count it pleasure to revel in the day-time, spots and blemishes, revelling in their deceivings while they feast with you;
having eyes full of adultery, and that cannot cease from sin; enticing unstedfast souls; having a heart exercised in covetousness; children of cursing;
forsaking the right way, they went astray, having followed the way of Balaam the son of Beor, who loved the hire of wrong-doing;
but he was rebuked for his own transgression: a dumb ass spake with man’s voice and stayed the madness of the prophet.
These are springs without water, and mists driven by a storm; for whom the blackness of darkness hath been reserved.
For, uttering great swelling words of vanity, they entice in the lusts of the flesh, by lasciviousness, those who are just escaping from them that live in error;
promising them liberty, while they themselves are bondservants of corruption; for of whom a man is overcome, of the same is he also brought into bondage.

For if, after they have escaped the defilements of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, they are again entangled therein and overcome, the last state is become worse with them than the first.
For it were better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than, after knowing it, to turn back from the holy commandment delivered unto them.
It has happened unto them according to the true proverb, The dog turning to his own vomit again, and the sow that had washed to wallowing in the mire.

summary.title: CHAPTER 2 IN SUMMARY
paras: As there were false prophets in Israel, there will be false teachers among believers, secretly bringing in destructive heresies, even denying the Master who bought them. Many will follow their sensuality, and in greed they will exploit people with false words, but their judgment is not idle.

God did not spare angels who sinned, nor the ancient world in Noah's flood, nor Sodom and Gomorrah, yet He rescued Noah and righteous Lot; “the Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptation, and to keep the unrighteous under punishment.” These teachers are bold and willful, like irrational animals; they revel in pleasure in the daytime, have eyes full of adultery, entice unstable souls and follow the way of Balaam, who loved the wages of wrongdoing. They are springs without water, promising freedom while they themselves are slaves of corruption. It would have been better for them never to have known the way of righteousness than to turn back, like a dog returning to its vomit.

questions.label: OBSERVE
questions.text: What examples of God's judgment and rescue does Peter give in vv. 4–9, and how does he describe the false teachers in vv. 12–19?

questions.label: THEN
questions.text: In a world of lavish Roman banquets, how might teachers who promised liberty while themselves slaves of corruption (v. 19) have attracted followers?

questions.label: NOW
questions.text: What kinds of freedom offered in our culture might actually enslave, and how can a group help one another see the difference?

items.text: Scoffers in the Last Days
This is now, beloved, the second epistle that I write unto you; and in both of them I stir up your sincere mind by putting you in remembrance;
that ye should remember the words which were spoken before by the holy prophets, and the commandment of the Lord and Saviour through your apostles:
knowing this first, that in the last days mockers shall come with mockery, walking after their own lusts,
and saying, Where is the promise of his coming? for, from the day that the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation.
For this they wilfully forget, that there were heavens from of old, and an earth compacted out of water and amidst water, by the word of God;
by which means the world that then was, being overflowed with water, perished:
but the heavens that now are, and the earth, by the same word have been stored up for fire, being reserved against the day of judgment and destruction of ungodly men.
The Day of the Lord
But forget not this one thing, beloved, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.
The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some count slackness; but is longsuffering to you-ward, not wishing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.

But the day of the Lord will come as a thief; in the which the heavens shall pass away with a great noise, and the elements shall be dissolved with fervent heat, and the earth and the works that are therein shall be burned up.
Seeing that these things are thus all to be dissolved, what manner of persons ought ye to be in all holy living and godliness,
looking for and earnestly desiring the coming of the day of God, by reason of which the heavens being on fire shall be dissolved, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat?
But, according to his promise, we look for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness.
Final Words: Grow in Grace
Wherefore, beloved, seeing that ye look for these things, give diligence that ye may be found in peace, without spot and blameless in his sight.
And account that the longsuffering of our Lord is salvation; even as our beloved brother Paul also, according to the wisdom given to him, wrote unto you;

as also in all his epistles, speaking in them of these things; wherein are some things hard to be understood, which the ignorant and unstedfast wrest, as they do also the other scriptures, unto their own destruction.
Ye therefore, beloved, knowing these things beforehand, beware lest, being carried away with the error of the wicked, ye fall from your own stedfastness.
But grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ. To him be the glory both now and for ever. Amen.

summary.title: CHAPTER 3 IN SUMMARY
paras: This is Peter's second letter, to stir up their memory of the prophets' words and the Lord's commandment through the apostles. In the last days scoffers will come, following their own lusts and saying, “Where is the promise of his coming?” since everything continues as it was. They forget that the world was formed by God's word and destroyed by water, and that the present heavens and earth are reserved for fire and judgment. “One day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.” The Lord is not slow about His promise but patient, not wishing that any should perish but that all should come to repentance. The day of the Lord will come like a thief, and the heavens and earth will be dissolved, so believers should live holy and godly lives, looking for new heavens and a new earth in which righteousness dwells. They should be diligent to be found at peace, count the Lord's patience as salvation, as Paul also wrote in letters that some twist, and guard against error, growing “in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ.”

wrap.title: 2 Peter In Summary
paras: 2 Peter is a farewell letter. Peter knows his death is near, as the Lord had told him, and he wants to leave believers with reminders that will keep them steady after he is gone. Its three chapters move from growth in godliness, to a warning against false teachers, to confident hope in the Lord's return.

Chapter 1 emphasizes that God has given believers everything they need for life and godliness, and calls them to add virtue, knowledge, self-control, patience, godliness, kindness and love to their faith. Peter grounds this in the reliability of the message: he was an eyewitness of Christ's majesty at the Transfiguration, and the prophetic Scriptures were spoken by people moved by the Holy Spirit. Chapter 2 is a sharp warning against false teachers who will arise within the church, denying the Lord who bought them, exploiting believers for money and promising freedom while living in corruption. Peter reminds his readers that God judged fallen angels, the ancient world and Sodom and Gomorrah, but rescued Noah and Lot, so He knows how to rescue the godly and judge the wicked.

Chapter 3 answers scoffers who say Christ will never return. God's timing is not ours: with Him a thousand years are as one day, and His apparent delay is patience, giving time for repentance. The day of the Lord will come suddenly, and the present world will pass away, but believers look for new heavens and a new earth where righteousness dwells.

The message in one line: God's promises are trustworthy and Christ will certainly return, so believers should reject false teaching, live holy lives, and keep growing in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.
